In Canada, the changing seasons are inseperable from daily life, and serve as a reminder of time's passing. Seasonal change allows me to truly appreciate moments that I would not otherwise connect with as deeply. For example, in the heat of mid-July summer, I am able to be thankful for the warmth even if I may be ridden with mosquito bites. In the winter, I may find comfort in stepping into the warmth of my home, and develop a new-found wonder of modern heating systems. Weather and seasons are cornerstones of these important days for me, and these moments would lose some of their spark if not for cool weather.

In conclusion, seasonal weather plays an irreplacable role in much of what I enjoy about life in Canada, and this would be sacrificed if I lived in a place that is always warm. task_prompt: Are today's teen too busy?
response_text:
Today’s teens find themselves overwhelmed with a number of different aspects of their lives. In response to the question, “are today’s teens too busy?”, it is hence crucial that the affirmative viewpoint is analyzed and taken into consideration. 

To begin with, social pressures have resulted in significant mental health impacts, which occupy much of a teen’s developing brain and time. Such social pressures include peer pressure, academic pressure, and the fear of being “left out.” These result in lesser self esteem and confidence, which immediately result in increased levels of stress. When pre-occupied with these external stressors, teenagers can find themselves with feelings of depression and anxiety, which in turn make schoolwork pile up due to a lack of motivation. Therefore, an aspect of this viewpoint is a lack of accomodation for students with these mental health issues. 

Another argument proving today’s teenagers are too busy is the fact that this school work/academic pressure, mentioned in paragraph 2, is an immense workload on these developing teens. Specifically, in IB and Private School programs, this workload often appears to be more than most can handle, which comes as a result of misplanning by the administrations of these educational facilities. For instance, the scheduling of summative assignments can certainly be better managed; It is a common complaint that in such programs, a number of assignments and assessments will be scheduled all during the same week as opposed to spreading them out more over the course of a few weeks perhaps, which would allow for a less stressful and more manageable timeframe for teens to work around. Hence, it is evident that poor scheduling within their education causes a lack of free time, and in turn, a more stressful/busy lifestyle. 

Finally, teens today find themselves pre-occupied with the stress of finding independence at a young age. In North American culture, the custom is that an individual leave their household when they are 18 to pursue a college or university education. However, at this age, it is significant to note that though they may be considered older, the individual is still growing and developing as a teenager, and this stress (which now includes monetary/financial stresses and having to sustain a decent lifestyle) inadvertantly piles up. The teenager becomes so occupied with these factors of their life (as well as those mentioned in paragraphs 2 and 3), that it may become nearly impossible for them to find free time to themselves; Studies have shown that rest (this time taken to ones’ self) is extremely crucial to brain development, and a lack of it may have detrimental consequences. Thus, cultural norms also play an important role in creating busy lifestyles for today’s teens. 

To conclude, as a result of social pressures, faults in the educational system, and cultural norms, today’s teens are evidently too busy. Moving forward, increased collaboration amongst educational systems and mental health professionals may contribute to both resolving the issue as well as helping these teenagers.

This is an exploration of how the lives of teens today are busier than any other time in history due to factors like new technology, social life, school-home balance, and responsibilities.
       Firstly, teens have become abnormally social with the rise of social media. This has impacted their daily lives by allowing them to communicate with friends and colleagues outside of school or work environments. Thus calling for excessive amounts of time spent on checking emails from teachers and coworkers, replying to text messages from friends and family, as well as reading conversations of strangers or celebrities on media apps like twitter or threads. Furthermore, In  human history, communication has always been face to face, only being able to occur in real life settings. However, now that people can speak to each other in person and online, much more time is spent socialising, especially for teens who often seek social life and fun.
        Next, a teen today is occupied with balancing their school life and home life. Within the home, teens require leaving out time for connecting with family, completing chores, or indulging in a hobby. Additionally, aspects such as school work and extra curricular activities can come at a cross over, leaving full time students busy with managing between their daily tasks. All of these factors leave today's teens without much free time to enjoy themselves or relax, which could also have an impact on their rest and performance academically and professionally. 
       Finally, the responsibilities that come with being a teen are what keep them so busy in our modern society. As teens make a transition from adolescents to young adults, they gain various responsibilities that come to prepare them for the real world. This includes planning for their future careers and education. For example, developing the skills needed for success, volunteering, and working part-time jobs for experience. Also, teens can often feel motivated to become more independent as moving away from parents becomes more common. Steps like buying a car or working towards earning money for university leads them to the path of independence. 
         In conclusion, today's teens are incredibly busy with their transitioning lives, and at times it can be overly complex and overwhelming. Throughout the ages, teens have never been as busy as now, with aspects like media and immense amounts of socialising in both in person and online, as well as managing time with school work with extra curricular and domestic activities being the main factors. Along with this, the newly found responsibilities that teens are faced with including planning for their future careers and becoming financially independent, motivate their drive and focus. task_prompt: Are today's teen too busy?
response_text:
Nowadays, there is always something to do for teenagers. They have to go to school and afterwards they do their homework, they can go shopping in the city, they can meet their friends, they can execute their hobby or spend time on their phone or computer. There is no such thing as boredom anymore, because there are a lot of more options for teenagers to do than there were years ago.

First of all, the school plays a very important role in the life of a teenager. School starts most of the time at 8 am and then they stay there until noon. If the school ends at 3 pm, they are already 5 hours occupied every week-day. In addition, they have to do their homework, which takes up two to three additional hours, and learn for upcoming tests. The only two free days, teenagers have, are Saturday and Sunday, but they still have to do work for school and a lot of parents expect their children to get goods grades in school, what puts additional pressure on them to do more for school to get even better grades.

But students have also hobbies, co-corriculars or clubs they want to do. It depends on what it is - and if it is a sport, if it's competitive or only recreational -, but these are one to two hours long and sometimes also require extra work, that has to be done too. When they are in a school, where it's mandatory or that strongly encourages the students to do a least one thing every term, like e.g. the Ashbury college, the teenagers come home at 5 o'clock. A full day can be very draining but after that, they still have to do their homework and other things, like helping their parents in the household. A lot of times, they have to continue working until late in the night. When having that full schedule every single day, it is also very hard to also have a social life or stay in contact with your friends. Of course, they can use facetime or WhatsApp to chat, but it is completely different to physically meeting them  and doing something together.

Another important factor in this issue is the internet. When teenagers are done with all their mandatory things, they usually watch a show on their IPad, computer or on the TV, go on their phone and scroll through Instagram or TikTok or chat with friends. Teenagers have always somthing to do and are therefore overstimulated. They never experience that feeling of boredom, because even if they have nothing to do, they can just do something on their phone that entertaines them. The internet opened a lot of options for everybody, who has access to it, but it has also a lot of negative consequences.

In a nutshell, there are a lot of options for teenagers in these days and having constant stimulation can also have negative consequences. If teenagers never rest and do nothing, their body can never get the relaxation it needs.
